exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Getting Ready for the Typhoon
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Have you heard the news, Sam? A strong typhoon is coming tonight.
Sam: Yes, the forecast says it will reach our city after midnight.
Lily: We should buy enough water and some food that doesn't need cooking.
Sam: Good idea. I'll also buy some batteries in case the power goes off.
Lily: Don't forget to bring the plants inside and close all the windows.
Sam: Right. My dad said we should tape the big windows so the glass won't break.
Lily: And we must stay indoors once it starts. The streets won't be safe.
Sam: Agreed. Let's keep the radio on for the latest announcements.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 告诉 Sam 今晚有强台风;预报说午夜后到城;两人决定买足够的水和免煮食物、买电池以防停电;把植物搬进屋、关好窗;Sam 的爸爸说要给大窗户贴胶带以防玻璃碎;台风一来就待在室内、开着收音机听最新公告。

questions.stem: When will the typhoon reach the city?

options: In case the power goes off.

options: Taping them so the glass won't break.

questions.stem: What must they do once the typhoon starts?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 How a Tsunami Forms
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A tsunami is one of the most dangerous events in the sea.
Most tsunamis are caused by a strong earthquake under the ocean floor.
When the sea floor suddenly moves, it pushes a huge amount of water upward.
This water travels across the ocean as fast as a plane, but in deep water the waves are still quite low.
Only when the waves reach shallow water near the coast do they grow into giant walls of water, so people must move to high ground as soon as a warning is given.
exercises.translation_cn: 海啸是海上最危险的事件之一;大多数海啸由海底强烈地震引起;海底突然移动时,会把大量海水向上推;这股水以飞机般的速度横越大洋,但在深水区浪还很低;只有当波浪到达海岸边的浅水区才会长成巨墙般的水墙,所以一旦发出警报,人们必须立刻转移到高处。

questions.stem: What causes most tsunamis?
options: A strong earthquake under the ocean floor.

questions.stem: How fast does the water travel across the ocean?
options: As slow as a person walking.
It does not move at all.

questions.stem: In deep water, what are the waves like?
When do the waves grow into giant walls of water?
options: When they reach shallow water near the coast.

questions.stem: What must people do when a warning is given?
options: Move to high ground at once.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 An Earthquake Survivor's Story
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Mr Li, can you tell us what you remember about the earthquake?
Mr Li: It happened so fast. The ground shook, and our house came down in seconds.
Anna: That sounds terrible. How did you and your family escape?
Mr Li: We were lucky. A rescue team pulled us out from under the broken walls.
Anna: How long did you have to wait before help came?
Mr Li: About two days, but it felt like months in the dark.
Anna: What kept you going during that time?
Mr Li: My wife kept saying that as long as we were together, there was still hope.
Anna: And how is life now?
Mr Li: Now we are rebuilding our home, and many kind strangers have helped us.
exercises.translation_cn: 记者 Anna 采访地震幸存者李先生;地震发生极快,房子几秒就塌了;一支救援队把全家从断墙下救出;他们等了约两天才等到救援,黑暗中却觉得像几个月;支撑他的是妻子常说的——只要一家人在一起就还有希望;如今他们正在重建家园,许多好心的陌生人也帮助了他们。

questions.stem: What happened to Mr Li's house?
options: It was moved to a new street.

options: A rescue team pulled them out.

options: As long as they were together, there was still hope.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Forecasting with Satellites
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: For thousands of years, people have tried to predict the weather.
Long ago, they watched the clouds, the wind and even the behaviour of animals.
Today, satellites high above the Earth send back pictures of storms while they are still far out at sea.
Computers then use this data to work out where a storm will go and how strong it will be.
Thanks to these tools, scientists can now forecast dangerous weather far more precisely, and a warning sent out in time can save thousands of lives.
exercises.translation_cn: 几千年来人们一直试图预测天气;很久以前,他们靠观察云、风,甚至动物的行为;如今,高悬地球上空的卫星在风暴还远在海上时就传回它们的图像;计算机再用这些数据算出风暴的去向和强度;借助这些工具,科学家如今能更精确地预报危险天气,而及时发出的警报能挽救成千上万的生命。

questions.stem: How did people predict the weather long ago?
options: By watching clouds, wind and animals.

questions.stem: What do satellites send back?
options: Pictures of storms far out at sea.

questions.stem: What do computers use the satellite data for?
options: To draw maps of the past.
To work out where a storm will go and how strong it will be.

questions.stem: What can scientists do better now than before?
What can a warning sent out in time do?

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 A Call About the Heatwave
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mr Brown: Hello, I'm calling to check how long this heatwave will last.
Ms Green: Good afternoon. I'm afraid it will continue for at least three more days.
Mr Brown: That's worrying. The temperature has already reached forty degrees here.
Ms Green: Yes, it's exceptionally hot. Please drink plenty of water and stay out of the sun.
Mr Brown: My grandmother feels dizzy. Is there anything I can do to help her?
Ms Green: Keep her in a cool room and give her cool water. If she gets worse, call a doctor.
Mr Brown: Thank you. Will there be any rain soon?
Ms Green: Some rain is expected at the weekend, which should make things cooler.
exercises.translation_cn: Brown 先生致电气象站,询问热浪还会持续多久;Green 女士说至少还有三天;当地气温已达四十度;她提醒多喝水、避开阳光;Brown 的祖母头晕,Green 建议让老人待在凉爽房间、喝凉水,若加重就叫医生;周末预计有雨,天气会转凉。

questions.stem: Why is Mr Brown calling the weather station?
options: To check how long the heatwave will last.

options: Drink plenty of water and stay out of the sun.

options: Take her out into the sun.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 A Message of Hope
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: When a disaster strikes, it can take away our homes, but it cannot take away our courage.
All around the world, people who have lost almost everything still find the strength to start again.
Neighbours share food and shelter, strangers send money and clothes, and rescue teams travel from faraway countries to help.
Little by little, broken towns come back to life, and new homes rise where old ones once stood.
A disaster shows us how powerful nature can be, but it also shows that human kindness and hope can shine even in the darkest of times.
exercises.translation_cn: 灾难袭来时,它能夺走我们的家园,却夺不走我们的勇气;世界各地,失去几乎一切的人仍能找到重新开始的力量;邻里分享食物与庇护,陌生人寄来钱物,救援队从遥远的国度赶来相助;一点一点地,破碎的城镇重新焕发生机,新家在旧址上拔地而起;灾难让我们看到自然的强大,也让我们看到——人间的善意与希望,即使在最黑暗的时刻也能闪光。
